text: Unleash my strength.
I'm ready to track.
Flush them out.
What lies before me?
My quarry nears.
The beasts obey me.
Where I lay my head is home. See that rock? That's my pillow.
The beasts around me are nothing compared to the beast within.
I will now summon the effete Dwayne-Two!
I summon the... Ah!
Don't have a cow. Oh, dear. Oops. Please bear with me. Oh, rats!
Unleash the beast!
By fang and claw!
Mangy cur!
I've got the scent.
On the prowl.
Our paths converge.
I'm acting on instinct.
I wander alone.
I hear the call of the wild.
For the Mog Nathal!
I have wandered alone for many years, little Misha. Yet sometimes even I grow weary of this endless solitude.
I have watched the other races. I have seen their squabbling, their ruthlessness. Their wars do nothing but scar the land and drive the wild things to extinction.
No, they cannot be trusted. Only beasts are above deceit.
A battle.
Hold fast, stranger. You shall not stand alone.
Your stomach's been split open. I can do little to ease your pain.
Failure.
I will deliver your message, old one. For the sake of honor, I will uphold your charge.
May the winds bear you swiftly to your ancestors, warrior.
Well, Misha, it seems we'll be seeing civilization after all. Let's get moving.
A warrior city. I have not seen its like in many years.
Stay close to me, Misha.
I carry a message for your war chief. I'll not stay long.
A moment, Warchief. I come to deliver a message.
He fell in the wilds. His last wish was that you receive this message.
I am Rexxar, last son of the mogu Nath'hal.
Perhaps I have spent too long in the wilds. Your offer is kind, thrall, but I must carry my own weight. Just show me what needs doing, and I'll earn my keep.
This must be one of the caravans Nazgrel told me about.
I never intended to chase you out. I intend to bury you here.
Thunder Ridge. This must be the valley Drek'thar spoke of. This shouldn't be too difficult.
This must be the Shimmer Reed. I'll need to gather five more bushels.
You're not paying me at all, little goblin.
This must be the entrance to the goblins' tunnels.
Do you goblins have a plan?
This must be one of the support beams. It's all yours, goblins.
This village has been razed. There's no evidence that the clan survived at all.
These tracks indicate that the lizards came through this pass. I'm curious as to where it leads.
Apparently, many of the Thunderlizards came from this secluded valley. I wonder what could have driven them out.
Humans. What could they be doing here?
A human lumber mill. They've cut down all of the trees. That's got to be what's driving the thunder lizards mad. We should destroy the mill immediately.
The poor beasts have been slain. What a terrible waste of life. We should report back to Thrall. He'll need to know what the humans are doing out here.
Now I can activate the telescope and survey the surrounding lands.
Blast! It looks like the beginnings of an invasion. There's far too many of them for me to handle alone.
This must be the entrance to the Quillbor's den. It smells foul enough. I don't even want to imagine what they're cooking in there.
It appears that they worship some kind of primitive boar god. Interesting.
No, we're too late. The camp's already been raised. There are human tracks everywhere. They lead back towards the coast.
No doubt about it. Those are the same ships I saw from the observatory.
This anchor emblem on their shields. Have you ever seen it before?
There's no telling what dangers lurk on these isles. I'll have to move quickly and find the trolls' village.
You have little chance of defeating such a force on your own, Vol'jin. You should evacuate your tribe to the mainland and unite with the Warchief's forces.
I have no flying mount, Vol'jin. I'll be useless on land.
We have no flying mounts, Vol'jin. We'll be useless on land.
Damn, the brazier is guarded by some kind of sea giant. Getting to it won't be as easy as I thought.
Whoa, he's a big one. I'm in for a serious fight.
I'll have to fight my way past that beast.
That vile creature stands in my way.
I hate to see any beast harmed, but there's no other way.
I don't know, Thrall. It sounds like a trap to me. Let me go in your place.
Just trust me. If you're right, we'll have lost nothing.
Worried? Bah! I'm just biding my time.
This is it. The meeting place lies just beyond.
Greetings, humans. It's about time you showed up.
And you are not Jaina Proudmoore.
Assassins! I knew this was a trap!
You're just in time, brothers. I saved a few of them for you.
Tell me who sent you, human. Was it Jaina?
You can count on me, Thrall. But I may need help bypassing the humans' defenses.
"Jaina Proudmoore, I am Rexxar. I bear a message from Warchief Thrall, the same Warchief you tried to kill. He is curious as to why your warriors encroach on our lands and threaten us with war."
Perhaps. But the fact remains that your ships and your warriors have been raiding our encampments on the mainland. I had to bypass a large encampment just to reach you.
Those snake creatures! They must have destroyed the camp and slaughtered your brethren.
Strange. I don't see any human bodies strewn around.
The serpent's lair must be around here somewhere. If we can find the human survivors, we'll confirm whether or not they serve your cause.
We're too late. The serpents already killed them all.
But what?
I don't understand. What's this all about?
Father.
I've got to get out of here and warn Thrall about Admiral Proudmoore. There are a number of small ships in the harbor. If I can commandeer one, I should be able to reach the open seas unnoticed.
This should do nicely. Now all I have to worry about are the harbor gates.
Proudmoore's marines have closed the harbor gates. I'll need to bust them open before I can escape. If I can make it to the open seas, I should have no problem reaching the mainland.
This beautiful land must be Mulgore. I have never met a Tauren before, but their strength and courage are legendary.
I come in the name of Thrall, Warchief of the Horde. His lands are in danger, and he calls upon his old allies to aid him. I seek the one known as Cairne. Do you know him?
Rotting kodo husks. What a terrible waste. The harpies will pay for this sacrilege of nature!

Greetings, brother Wintotem. I was told you could help me locate Chieftain Bloodhoof's son. There may still be a chance that the boy lives, but we'll need to find the centaur encampment as quickly as possible.
That's the centaur encampment. They could be keeping Bane in one of those cages, but we'll have to fight our way to them.
Don't worry, Bane. We'll have you back to your father in no time.
New warlord, huh? Don't worry, friend. I think I can help you. Have your witch doctors tend to his wounds, Vol'jin. I'm going to pay a little visit to his clan and meet this new warlord for myself.
That must be the ogre's village. I should fit right in.
Look, I don't want any trouble. I just want to talk with your warlord.
I've uh, come to join your clan. I want to be a stonemaul too.
This must be the valley Korgal spoke of. The Gauntlet, he called it. Well, I'd better get this over with. I'd hate to keep the brute waiting.
I want you and your warriors to help the horde battle the humans. The Stonemaul clan would be a great asset to the orc warchief.
Then perhaps you've ruled long enough.
Korgal, as a member of the Stonemaul clan, I claim the right to challenge you for leadership.
I underestimated Korgal's skills. I'll need to call upon my beasts to defeat him.

I have defeated Korgal in single combat. I have passed the trial of blood. I rule Stonemaul Clan now, and I command you all to war! You ogres arm yourselves and meet the orc warchief upon the plains. Blood and glory to the Stonemaul clan!
Of course, Thrall. I'd be proud to.
I've secured the first component, but I've got to hurry and get the others. Time is running out.
That's it. I've got all of them. I'd better get these back to Thrall quickly.
It is an honor, Warchief. I will carry your standard with pride. LOK'TAR OGA!
Gladly. All right, you warriors. The hour of victory has arrived. Come, you Tauren. Rise up, you Ogres. Today, you stand united with the Horde. Lok'tar Ogar!
Strike hard, warriors! Push the humans back!
Slay the invaders. Let none survive!
The human lines are breaking. Now is our time to strike.
Thrungar, Warchief, we've routed the human forces on the mainland, but it appears that Admiral Proudmoore and his marines have pulled back to the safety of Theramore Isle.
Warchief, our troops are ready, but the admirals assembled a blockade of battleships around Theramore. There's no way we can match their firepower.
Our forces are ready, Thrall. It's now or never.
There, the goblin shipyard Janus spoke of. Now we can hire the juggernauts to help us break the blockade.
The blockade is broken. Board the transports quickly! We must land on Theramore and crush the admiral's defenses.
Jaina's warriors are attacking! Remember our oath to her. Defend yourselves against them, but spare their structures.
Thank you, Warchief. Now only one task remains. We must storm the citadel and deal with Admiral Proudmoore once and for all.
Lok'tar Ogar! For the horde! For Durotar!
The admiral's elite guard are trying to cut us off. Slay them all!
It's over. Stand down, humans.
Above all else, Jaina, he was a proud warrior. Remember him as such.

I appreciate your offer, Thrall, but I am Mok'nathal, a wanderer. I belong in the wilds amidst the beasts and elements of the land. But know this, brother. I will always be a part of the horde. I will always be there when you need me. Farewell.
This place reeks of evil. It must be where the warlocks are hiding.
What the hell is that stuff? Are you trying to kill me?
Not at all, Chen. But my path is a perilous one.
